scope: Fresh 4D-STEM scan from the February graphene series. Supplementary Table 4 identifies it with Supplementary Fig. 8 and reports a local twist range of 0.999 to 1.7399 degrees in the triangulated region. The 1.2592 degree catalogue mean describes the scan, and every scored wall is assigned its local geometry from first-ring data. Treat this as a new acquisition within the same publication and instrument.

inputs.microscope: Nominal 1.3 nm probe for the February series. Use the authors' aperture at 2.662 pixels for the primary readout and 3.5 pixels for sensitivity. Use the same intensity response and isolated-profile observer as the prior graphene study.

qualification.intensity_correlation_scope: Apply the 0.30 gate to both rings independently within each prespecified window. If a window spans the tear or the phase recovery fails, report its reason and geometry diagnostics. The intensity correlation is a signal check. Independently report width differences across opposite spot groups.
qualification.window_selection: Four fixed overlapping windows cover the scan. Reject chords without four observed AA neighbors and controls in the existing observer. Use first-ring coherence and center geometry throughout. Deduplicate overlapping windows by a 1.5 nm midpoint match and matching wall direction within 20 degrees, keeping the chord furthest from a window edge. Never select by measured second-ring gap or model performance.
qualification.within_scan_spacing_groups: Compare the shortest and longest thirds of geometry-selected spacings. Assign thirds before excluding any width fits. This compares the range in this scan even if no wall reaches the wider 15 nm group.

score.prediction: Compare fixed periodic relaxation with the exact isolated-wall model and the source-ring-fitted isolated shape using the existing procedure. The new near-tear scan uses a local periodic solve at each qualifying window's measured geometry, retaining the per-chord affine sampling. Measure the signed first-minus-second width gap; score full profiles from one ring to the other in both directions. Always report the repeatability from separate sets of opposite Bragg spots and both aperture sizes.
score.claim: For numeric agreement on the new high-twist regions, require at least six qualified common walls, an advantage over the exact isolated-wall baseline in both profile directions, and a median gap error within 0.5 nm or the opposite-spot disagreement if larger, as in the parent protocol. For a more predictive width measurement, report the stricter 0.5 nm result separately. Compare the groups and spacing thirds in the same acquisition and retain their individual scores. The walls do not supply independent specimens.
